analysis_md:
# PEG — Public Service Enterprise Group Incorporated
v5 run, 2026-10-14 (supersedes the 2026-10-13 v4-era analysis; under v5 the prior hand-built TTM operating-earnings base is not used — see STALE_FY below). In scope (market cap $35.305B at $70.47, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Operating-EPS and guidance figures are from cited search results (Q2 2026 release / call), as noted.

## What it is
Newark-based holding company for PSE&G, New Jersey's largest regulated electric and gas utility (~2.4M electric, ~1.9M gas customers per search results), PSEG Power (merchant generation dominated by nuclear — Salem and Hope Creek in NJ plus a stake in Peach Bottom, PA, ~3,758 MW in total), and PSEG Long Island (operations provider for LIPA). The regulated business is the earnings anchor: a $22.5–$25.5B regulated capex plan through 2030, rate base guided to a 6–7.5% CAGR, and a planned base-rate filing by year-end 2026. Management reaffirmed 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS guidance of $4.28–$4.40 with Q2 2026 results and a long-term operating-EPS growth target of 6–8% through 2030 (search results).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $12,168M; net income $2,111M; operating cash flow $3,298M; capex $3,272M (tag: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $43M (tag: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$17M = −$0.03/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total −$17.0M, latest FY OE/share −$0.03). Capex consumes essentially all of operating cash flow — structural for a rate-base-growing utility, not a one-off year.
- **OE positive 1 of the last 5 fiscal years** (key_numbers.md): FY2021 −$1,011M / FY2022 −$1,414M / FY2023 +$463M / FY2024 −$1,287M / FY2025 −$17M, from financials_history.csv.
- Maintenance version: the engine leaves it blank from 2019 onward in financials_history.csv (no usable annual D&A series in the pulled facts), so no maintenance figure is quoted here — per the sweep rule, a figure not in the computed outputs is stated in words, not calculated. In words: the gap between the definitions is the story — most utility capex is growth capex that enters rate base and earns an allowed return, so the conservative definition (OCF − total capex − SBC) is the harsher yardstick, and it is the sweep's base case.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): −$0.03/share** (key_numbers.md: base OE/share −$0.03, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY alone is also −$0.03/share). Both are ≤ 0, so the choice does not change the verdict. No TTM base was used — see STALE_FY below.
- Balance sheet: net debt $22.413B (key_numbers.md). Shares diluted (latest): 501,000,000.

## Moat: 6/10 — durable legal monopoly plus a scarce nuclear fleet, capped economics
Justification: Legal monopoly NJ transmission and distribution franchise (PSE&G, ~2.4M electric and ~1.9M gas customers) with essential, inelastic demand and a $22.5–$25.5B regulated capex plan through 2030 guided to 6–7.5% rate-base CAGR, plus NJ's only nuclear fleet (~3,758 MW, scarce, with PJM capacity upside) and a plan management says is fundable with no new equity. Capped at 6 because the NJ BPU sets allowed returns (no pricing power, affordability-exposed base-rate filing due by year-end 2026), merchant nuclear lost ZEC support in May 2025 and is hedged not contracted long-term, growth is debt-funded (net debt $22,413M), and the gas network faces long-run electrification risk.
- FOR: Legal monopoly NJ T&D franchise — PSE&G serves ~2.4M electric / ~1.9M gas customers, essential inelastic demand; regulated capex $22.5–25.5B through 2030 guided to 6–7.5% rate-base CAGR, largely clause-recovered; scarce nuclear fleet ~3,758 MW — NJ's only nuclear operator, PJM capacity and data-center load optionality; 5-yr plan fundable with no new equity per management, dividend raised with 2026 indicative $2.68/share (search results).
- AGAINST: BPU caps allowed returns — no pricing power, affordability-exposed base-rate filing planned by year-end 2026; merchant nuclear unsubsidized after ZECs ended May 2025 — hedged (~95% for 2026 per search results), not contracted long-term, GAAP swings with mark-to-market; debt-funded growth — net debt $22.413B at YE2025, equity absorbs any disallowance or rate lag first; long-run gas-network electrification / decarbonization risk, data-center / nuclear premium discussed not contracted.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years by the sweep formula — academic here, since there is no positive OE stream to fade (key_numbers.md records CAP as None on this F run).

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
The final engine pass was run with moat 6 and default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25), but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the normalized base OE is −$0.03/share, so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F**.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Adverse rate case, affordability caps bite | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Capex stays at/above OCF | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | Capex ≈ OCF indefinitely; OE ≈ 0 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | Rate-base growth converts to FCF sooner than history suggests | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Structural FCF inflection | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the engine's blended growth is 7.48% (key_numbers.md components: rev CAGR 5y 4.85%, rev CAGR 3y 7.48%, latest rev YoY 18.25%, OE/share CAGR 2y —). That blend sits in line with management's guided 6–8% operating-EPS growth through 2030 (search results), but growth is irrelevant to the verdict: it multiplies a negative base. The latest rev YoY of 18.25% is a revenue print, not per-share earning power, and is not used to lift any scenario.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS $0.86 vs $0.77 a year earlier; GAAP net income $0.67 vs $1.17 (mark-to-market / reconciling items and the end of ZEC payments in May 2025); H1 2026 operating EPS $2.41 vs $2.20; nuclear cleared ~3,600 MW at $325/MW-day in PJM for the 2028 delivery year and ran at a 92% capacity factor in Q2. The earnings engine is healthy — it is the capex load, not profitability, that zeroes out conservative OE.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 2025-12-31, 9 months ago): ttm.py was run and **exited non-zero**: "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for PEG (CIK 788784): sbc: no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end)" — PEG's 10-Q facts do not give ttm.py a usable post-FY YTD SBC leg, so no TTM base exists and no ttm.json was saved. Per the sweep rules, the engine's median base (−$0.03/share) is used instead, with the reason stated here. This does not change the outcome: the latest full FY is also ≤ 0 (−$0.03/share), and the Q2/H1 2026 prints above give no indication capex has fallen below OCF. The v4-era hand-built TTM operating-earnings base ($4.26/share) is therefore NOT carried forward under v5 — v5 requires a ttm.py-derived pin or a declared base_override, and neither exists here.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Utilities): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits regulated utilities poorly, because growth capex is rate-base investment earning a regulated return, not value destruction. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier is read as "not modelable on this screen," not as "bad business."

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is the model's known blind spot, flagged as such: PEG is a profitable, dividend-growing regulated monopoly whose conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years because utility capex runs at or near operating cash flow every year. The dividend is funded the utility way — rate recovery plus continuous debt issuance — which an OE screen reads as ~zero distributable cash.
- On numbers a utility investor actually uses (from search results, not the engine): 2026 operating EPS guided $4.28–$4.40 at a $70.47 price, long-term operating-EPS growth guided 6–8% through 2030, rate base guided 6–7.5%. That is a bond-like mid-to-high-single-digit equity return profile before any multiple change — nowhere near Andrew's 15% hurdle on any defensible reading, so the F here happens to agree with the hurdle conclusion even though the model's mechanism (negative OE) is a sector artifact. No method range spanning tiers is claimed: on the v5 method there is one result, F, and the prior v4 D (9.9% on a hand-built operating-earnings base) is superseded, not averaged in.
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable from this model — with no positive OE base there is no IV@15% at any price, and stating one would require a different model (dividend/rate-base), which is out of scope for this sweep. No tier override: the numbers tier F is retained, with the mismatch documented, rather than inventing a tier the v5 method cannot support.
- Real risks for a holder (outside the model): NJ affordability politics in the planned year-end 2026 base-rate filing, merchant nuclear earnings after ZEC expiry (hedged, not contracted), and leverage (net debt $22.413B) refinanced at current rates.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F — no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings; OE DCF not supportable)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch: the F is a model artifact for a regulated utility, though no alternative reading clears a 15% hurdle either)
- One-liner: Durable NJ regulated monopoly plus scarce nuclear fleet, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years (capex consumes ~all of OCF; normalized base -$0.03/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided 6-8% operating EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
